answer: Because the mesa index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the pulse audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a fable index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Filling 44 aliases therefore needs 44 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
